title: MotionStyleTemplateRecord
description: Layer 6 of the component model: the decision unit for 'what should this video look like'. A style template is a versioned contract for one kind of visual job (explain a mechanism, build a proof, show a quantity, ...). It BINDS a style system (paint: tokens and CSS) and a design profile (DNA: identity, motion, camera, audio) and adds what neither has: when to pick it, the scene grammar, measurable production rules that studio.py checks before a render, anti-patterns learned from reviews, and a revision log. Refine the template and every project that subscribes to it is flagged as behind. It never repeats colours, fonts or easing; those stay in the style system.

version.description: Bumped on every change that alters what a conforming video looks like or what is checked. Must equal the highest version in `revisions`. Projects pin the version they were built against.

visual_job.description: What the picture has to do. This, more than the subject, decides which template fits.

kind.description: mechanism: how parts interact. proof: an abstract argument built step by step. quantity: how much, and how it changes. sequence: what happened, in what order, where. narrative: people, stakes and an emotional arc. evidence: what is known, from whom, how sure. natural-world: physical structure, scale and process.

viewer_leaves_able_to.description: The one thing the viewer can do or say afterwards.

hero.description: What is on screen most of the time.

categories.description: Subject categories (specs/categories.json) this template usually serves. A hint, not a gate: the visual job decides.

keywords.description: Lower-case words and short phrases that, found in a brief's objective, message or tone, point to this template. Used by `studio.py style recommend`.

style.description: Default style system (catalogue/data/styles/). Light unless the brief asks otherwise.

when.description: The condition that justifies leaving the default.

design_profile.description: Registry design profile (catalogue/data/design-profiles/) that supplies camera, transition and audio DNA.

scene_grammar.description: The reusable scene roles of this kind of film and the visual formula for each. A storyboard is a sequence of these.

capabilities.description: Catalogue ids (primitives, effects, recipes, compositions) that usually build this role.

signature.description: The one motion idea that makes a film of this kind recognisable.

continuous_layer.description: What keeps the frame alive between events (the per-scene drift layer).

rules.description: Measurable production rules. Each one is checked by `studio.py style check` against storyboard.json, narration and audio/timeline.json, before any render.

hook_within_sec.description: The hero is on screen and a first beat lands by this time.

max_beat_gap_sec.description: Longest stretch inside a scene without a planned visual event (storyboard beats).

max_scene_sec.description: A scene longer than this must be split or carry storyboard beats; once it has beats, max_beat_gap_sec governs it.

words_per_10s_max.description: Narration budget per scene, words per 10 s of measured clip. Fix by cutting words, not by raising speed.

ending.description: How the film must close. Judged in review; not machine-checked.

short_form.description: Extra rules for reel-length, portrait-first delivery (a project whose only or primary format is portrait). Optional.

max_card_words.description: Longest on-screen text item, in words. A card is read at arm's length before the viewer is listening. Checked against storyboard on_screen_text by `studio.py style check`.

closing.description: How a reel-length film closes so a replay lands cleanly (for example, echo a word or image from the hook). Judged in review; `studio.py script` checks the word echo.

anti_patterns.description: Mistakes that were seen, each traced to the review or render that showed it.

source.description: Project, review or memory note that evidenced it.

reference_projects.description: Existing projects that approximate this template, for calibration. Listing one is not a claim that it conforms.

open_questions.description: Known gaps. A template is honest about what it has not settled.

reason.description: The evidence that prompted it: a review, a render, a measured result.
